messages:
maya: Quick sync — I'm drafting the PRD for rate limits / quotas / billing semantics. Need alignment on MVP scope, acceptance criteria, and tricky edge cases before I ship the doc to legal/finance.

maya: Goal: define metering & limits that work across Hosted / Dedicated / Private (same semantics where possible), and produce an API + Console design + billing event spec.

maya: Key questions I'm trying to answer in this PRD:
- Pricing unit(s): per-token (in/out) vs per-request vs hybrid
- Rate-limits: RPS, concurrent requests, per-model and per-customer tiers
- Quotas: monthly usage caps, daily budgets, soft/hard thresholds and grace behavior
- Metering accuracy for streaming & batching
- UI/UX: how teams see usage & estimated costs
- Billing integration: real-time metering vs batch invoice events

james: +1 — can we clearly separate "metering" (what we count) from "billing semantics" (how we translate counts to $)? That helps Dedicated/private customers who want different pricing.

sandeep: Implementation notes from infra perspective:
- Metering must be tied to the final tokenization used by the model variant serving the request (so quantization or model-size shouldn't change token counts, but model truncation/prefix caching will).
- For streaming: count tokens as they are produced, but only emit billing events once the response is finalized or every N seconds for long streams.
- Batching: we should meter per-request within a batch (i.e., attribute tokens to original request IDs). We do not want to bill a batch as a single monolithic token blob.

sandeep: Possible API headers / response snippets we can expose today:
```
X-RW-Quota-Limit: 2000000   # monthly token quota
X-RW-Quota-Remaining: 150234
X-RW-RateLimit-Limit: 50    # requests per minute
X-RW-RateLimit-Reset: 1719990000
```

emily: From billing side — we need a clean invoice/event model. Proposal:
- Metering output: events with fields: {customer_id, org_id, model_name, request_id, input_tokens, output_tokens, timestamp}
- Aggregate daily for invoice lines. Keep raw events for 90 days for audits.
- Overage policy: bill automatically at pay-as-you-go rates, plus email & web warning at 80% and 95% of quota.
- Proration: if a customer upgrades mid-billing-cycle, prorate quotas and reserved capacity charges.

olivia: UX notes:
- Console should show per-route and per-model cost estimate (last 7d, forecast for month). Click-to-expand shows sample requests contributing the cost.
- Quotas page: allow admins to set soft cap (warn), hard cap (block), and weekly budget. Default behavior: soft cap -> throttling + warnings; hard cap -> 429/block.
- For Dedicated: expose the same controls but note that local-only enforcement (customer-configurable) may be required for Private.

maya: Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Define canonical metering unit: input_tokens + output_tokens (tokens counted using model tokenizer for the model actually used).
- API: token headers (limit/remaining/reset) implemented for hosted API and documented in SDKs.
- Console: basic quota UI (monthly cap + remaining + thresholds) and alerts at 80%/95%.
- Billing: daily aggregated billing events available to finance, and overage handling defined.
- Back-compat: existing customers on legacy metering kept with an opt-in migration plan.

james: Scope negotiation: propose two-phase rollout:
- Phase 1 (MVP, 6 weeks): implement metering events, API headers, basic console, and default soft/hard threshold behavior for Hosted.
- Phase 2 (v1, 12 weeks): add per-route cost attribution, streaming edge-case fixes, Dedicated SLA integration, and Private deployment docs.

sandeep: Edge cases to call out in the PRD (we need test cases):
- Retries: when client retries a request due to network error, ensure we dedupe billing for retries if they were not processed (use request_id idempotency).
- Partial responses / cancellations: count tokens produced up until cancel; if model resumes later, attribute to same request_id.
- Model fallback: if we fall back to a cheaper model automatically, we must record which model served the request for billing.
- Batch cancellation: when a batch contains multiple requests and the batch fails, ensure per-request receipts show zero or full consumption based on whether served.

emily: Additions for billing:
- Provide a hook/export -> streaming Kafka topic with raw metering events for invoicing / audit.
- Require exported events to have checksum and sequence numbers for reconciliation.

maya: Example billing event (for PRD):
```
{
  "event_type": "usage",
  "timestamp": 1719987800,
  "customer_id": "org_123",
  "request_id": "req_9f7a",
  "model": "rw-open-1",
  "input_tokens": 42,
  "output_tokens": 256,
  "final": true
}
```

olivia: Console acceptance criteria:
- Admins can set soft and hard caps via UI and via Admin API.
- Warnings sent at 80%/95% by email and in-console.
- Historical drilldown: click a day -> list of top 50 requests by token count with timestamps.

james: Non-goals for MVP (call these out clearly in PRD):
- Fine-grained per-user seats billing (that's v2).
- Real-time chargebacks to external accounting systems (v2 export only).
- Automatic model-switching to minimize cost (ops feature v2).

sandeep: Implementation constraints:
- Metering service must be eventually consistent but provide <5s latency for emitted events for near-real-time alerts.
- For Private, offer a mode: "local metering" (events stored locally and exported) vs "central metering" (events sent to Redwood cloud). Document data flows.

maya: Final asks before I write the PRD:
- Engineering: confirm token-counting approach (per-model tokenizer, attribute to request_id) and confirm retry dedupe plan. — @sandeep
- Finance: confirm export format + retention (90 days raw events). — @emily
- Design: confirm console wireframes for quota page & alert flows. — @olivia
- PM: I'll produce the PRD draft by EOD Friday with MVP scope + acceptance criteria; want a quick review cycle Monday.

sandeep: Confirmed on token-counting approach. We'll use request_id idempotency + a short dedupe window (5 minutes) keyed by request_id + customer.

emily: Confirmed on export format + 90d retention. Also request adding an invoice_preview endpoint for customers to estimate next bill (v1)

olivia: Wireframes ready, will post links in thread tomorrow. Quick note: make sure quota page has clear explainer copy about "why counts may differ from local SDK estimates" :thinking_face:

maya: Thanks — I'll incorporate and @james will help with scoped rollout messaging. Putting a draft in the PRD repo shortly. :rocket:
